title.en: Enjoying the Wilderness in an Autumn Grove

institution.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
institution.credit_line: Bequest of John M. Crawford Jr., 1988

image.edit: Trimmed the dark photographic background around the object, then resized.

basis.en: Public domain: the artist died in 1374. The Metropolitan Museum of Art releases this image under CC0 through its Open Access programme.
basis.zh: 公有领域：作者卒于 1374 年。大都会艺术博物馆通过开放获取计划以 CC0 发布此图像。

alt.en: A spare ink landscape. A cluster of thin autumn trees grows from rounded rocks in the foreground, a small thatched pavilion stands at the water's edge behind them, and a calm river opens toward low hills. Inscriptions in several hands fill the paper above.
alt.zh: 一幅简淡的水墨山水。前景圆润的石头上长着一丛瘦削的秋树，树后水边立着一座小小的茅亭，平静的河面向低缓的远山展开。上方的纸面写满了不同人的题跋。

note.en: Ni Zan, one of the Four Masters of the Yuan, became famous for a few dry strokes, an empty pavilion and wide water; this early work, painted in his thirties, already has the habit. Later owners added their own poems above, so the scroll is also a long conversation about itself. Look at how much of the river is simply paper.
note.zh: 倪瓒是元四家之一，以寥寥干笔、一座空亭、一片阔水闻名；这件三十多岁时的早期作品已经有了这种习惯。后来的藏家在上方题了自己的诗，所以这幅画也是一场关于它自己的长谈。看看那条河有多少地方只是纸。
